Jonas / team — draft numbers and talking points below (kept concise so we can push this to Elena as one-pager + spreadsheet):

1) Hosted (baseline) — list prices (showing generation + embeddings):
- Generation (text gen): $0.0007 per token (list)
- Embeddings: $0.003 per 1K embedding units (list)
- Typical optimizations we assume: batching & KV-prefix cache can reduce effective gen cost by ~12–25% depending on prompt reuse

Example math (your footprint: 100M tokens / mo + 50k embeddings):
- Generation cost (list): 100,000,000 * $0.0007 = $70,000/mo
- Embeddings: 50,000 * $0.003 = $150/mo
- Hosted baseline total (list): ~$70.15k/mo

2) Dedicated (reserved capacity) — how it changes:
- Pricing model: committed monthly fee for a pool of GPU capacity + platform fee. We typically convert hosted unit consumption into an equivalent GPU-reserved SKU for quoting.
- Example translation (approx): to sustain 100M gen tokens with reasonable latency you can look at a 2–4 GPU reserved pool depending on model/seq length. Typical committed cost (illustrative): $18k–$36k/month for the GPU pool + $3k/mo platform fee = $21k–$39k/mo.
- Effective unit delta: when amortized, Dedicated often delivers ~25–45% lower per-token cost than hosted list depending on utilization and model choice.
- Discounts: we price Dedicated as committed (12/24/36 mo) — suggested net guidance: 12-mo commit => ~25% off hosted-equivalent; 24–36 mo => 35–45%.

3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — what to expect:
- One-time platform/license fee: typical range $50k–$120k depending on scope (VPC integration, audit requirements, HSM/KMS integration).
- Recurring platform fee: $2k–$6k/mo (manages control plane, telemetry, security integrations).
- Infra: customer pays for infra (on-prem) or we recommend cloud sizing (e.g., 4x A100 equiv = ~$XXk/mo infra). If Redwood manages the infra in a private cloud, we provide an infra estimate.
- PS/Onboarding: one-time professional services for deployment and runbooks — $15k–$40k typical.
- Private is best justified by compliance, data residency, or strict SLA/throughput needs; commercial discounts are at the high end once a license/platform fee is included.

4) Packaging & pragmatic options we recommend for FinOpsCloud:
- Start on Hosted to validate UX and initial traffic patterns (fast time-to-value).
- Move to Dedicated when steady baseline utilization emerges (commit drives lower unit cost).
- Private if SOC2 / VPC controls + audit evidence are gating procurement; include a one-time license + PS in the quote.
- Hybrid routing: route latency-sensitive traffic to Dedicated and less-sensitive to Hosted when there is burst — saves cost and reduces overcommit.

5) Sample pricing for FinOpsCloud (conservative mid-case) — monthly net (illustrative):
- Hosted (list): ~$70.2k/mo
- Hosted w/ negotiated 12-mo commit (25% net): ~$52.6k/mo
- Dedicated (2–3 GPU reserved pool + platform fee, 12-mo commit): ~$25k–30k/mo (~40% lower than hosted list)
- Private (one-time license + infra + recurring platform): Opex ~similar to Dedicated but add $50k–100k one-time + PS fees

6) Negotiation levers we typically use:
- Commit length and minimum spend (biggest lever for discounts)
- Inclusion of platform fee vs absorbed discount (we can move platform fee into a rebate for larger commits)
- SLOs and support package (higher SLA => higher pricing)

I’ll assemble the one-pager and a detailed xlsx with line items (unit math) — attaching the xlsx in the next message for Jonas to review. If they need SOC2/pen-test artifacts we should send the security team link.

—Marissa
